title_en: Huang Ming v. Chen Qiling, Chen Zefeng, Fujian Fengquan Environmental Protection Group Co., Ltd. — dispute over private lending
ruling_gist_en: The exercise of the right of set-off shall not harm the legitimate rights and interests of third parties. Where a creditor is simultaneously a judgment debtor in multiple enforcement cases and has no actual property to satisfy debts owed to others, and a debtor acquires the enforcement claim held by the applying enforcement creditor against the creditor and claims to set off the creditor's claim, the people's court shall review the acquisition of the active claim, to prevent the active claim from obtaining priority satisfaction in a disguised form, thereby harming the interests of other creditors. The enforcement claim acquired by the debtor shall still be realized through participation in distribution in the enforcement case where the creditor is the judgment debtor, so as to curb malicious set-off and maintain the private law order of fair satisfaction of claims.
keywords_en: Civil; private lending dispute; second instance; Supreme People's Court; Fujian Province; natural person; legal person; Contract Law; whether the exercise of the right of set-off harms the legitimate rights and interests of third parties; whether the acquisition of the active claim is lawful; fair satisfaction of claims; affirm the original judgment; private lending; assignment of claims; right of set-off; participation in distribution; principle of fairness; private lending dispute of a group company limited
full_text_en:
Huang Ming v. Chen Qiling, Chen Zefeng, and Fujian Fengquan Environmental Protection Group Co., Ltd. — dispute over private lending

【Ruling Summary】

The exercise of the right of set-off shall not impair the legitimate rights and interests of third parties. Where a creditor is simultaneously an enforcement respondent in multiple enforcement cases and has no actual property to satisfy the debts of others, and the debtor claims set-off against the creditor's claim by acquiring the enforcement claim held by the applying enforcement applicant against the creditor, the people's court shall examine the circumstances under which the active claim was acquired, so as to prevent the active claim from obtaining priority satisfaction in a disguised form, thereby prejudicing the interests of other creditors. The enforcement claim acquired by the debtor shall still be realized through participation in distribution in the enforcement case in which the creditor is the enforcement respondent, so as to curb malicious set-off and maintain the private law order of fair satisfaction of claims.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court

(2019) Supreme People's Court Final No. 218

Appellants (defendants at first instance): Chen Qiling, female, born on October 25, 1973, Han Chinese, residing in Gulou District, Fuzhou City, Fujian Province.

Appellants (defendants at first instance): Chen Zefeng, male, born on September 22, 1969, resident of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, contact address in mainland China: Fujian Fengquan Environmental Protection Group Co., Ltd.

Appellants (defendants at first instance): Fujian Fengquan Environmental Protection Group Co., Ltd., domiciled at: Fengquan Environmental Protection Group Science and Technology Park, Gaoshi Road, Cangshan District, Fuzhou City, Fujian Province.

Legal representative: Chen Zefeng, Chairman of the Board.

Jointly authorized agents ad litem of the above three appellants: Wang Jinzhang, lawyer of Grandall Law Firm (Fuzhou).

Jointly authorized agents ad litem of the above three appellants: Zhang Liming, lawyer of Grandall Law Firm (Beijing).

Respondent (plaintiff at first instance): Huang Ming, male, born on August 12, 1963, Han Chinese, residing in Siming District, Xiamen City, Fujian Province.

Authorized agent ad litem: Chen Zhiming, lawyer of Fujian Mingjia Law Firm.

Authorized agent ad litem: Yan Hong, lawyer of Fujian Mingjia Law Firm.

The appellants Chen Qiling, Chen Zefeng, and Fujian Fengquan Environmental Protection Group Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Fengquan Company), dissatisfied with the civil judgment (2016) Min Chu No. 106 rendered by the Fujian High People's Court (hereinafter referred to as Fujian High Court) in the dispute over private lending with the respondent Huang Ming, appealed to this Court. As Huang Ming failed to pay the appeal fee within the time limit, his appeal was deemed withdrawn. This Court accepted the case on February 13, 2019, and after forming a collegial panel, held a hearing. The jointly authorized agents ad litem of the appellants Chen Qiling, Chen Zefeng, and Fengquan Company, Wang Jinzhang and Zhang Liming, and the authorized agent ad litem of the respondent Huang Ming, Chen Zhiming, appeared in court. The trial period of this case was lawfully extended, and the case has now been concluded.

The appellants Chen Qiling, Chen Zefeng, and Fengquan Company appealed requesting: 1. To set aside the judgment (2016) Min Chu No. 106 of Fujian High Court and dismiss all of Huang Ming's claims; 2. To order Huang Ming to bear all litigation costs of the first instance and the appeal. The main facts and reasons are as follows: 1. The principal and interest of the debt in question were confirmed by the parties' "Settlement Plan" to be 40,000,000 yuan, not the amount determined in the judgment. On January 22, 2018, Huang Ming confirmed the principal and interest of the loan: as of December 31, 2017, the outstanding loan principal was 35,000,000 yuan, and the interest calculated at 2% amounted to 16,800,000 yuan. Finally, the parties agreed to settle at 40,000,000 yuan. The parties signed and thumbprinted the "Settlement Plan" printed by Huang Ming. Therefore, the principal and interest of the debt in question should be determined as a total of 40,000,000 yuan. Although Chen Qiling and Fengquan Company did not participate in signing the "Settlement Plan," they both approved it. 2. The debt in question has been set off, and the appeal should be granted to dismiss all of Huang Ming's claims. The dispute over private lending between the third party Wu Yongzhong and Huang Ming was finally adjudicated by the Xiamen Intermediate People's Court (hereinafter referred to as Xiamen Intermediate Court) and Fujian High Court in the second instance, resulting in effective civil judgments (2014) Xia Min Chu Zi No. 679 and (2015) Min Min Zhong Zi No. 2259. Wu Yongzhong has applied to Xiamen Intermediate Court for enforcement of the loan principal of 41,000,000 yuan and corresponding interest from Huang Ming. Chen Qiling acquired all of Wu Yongzhong's claims against Huang Ming in the aforementioned case. Wu Yongzhong has notified Huang Ming in writing of the assignment of the claims, and Huang Ming personally signed for the notice. Wu Yongzhong also informed the enforcement court of the assignment. According to Articles 79 and 80 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Contract Law), the assignment of claims has taken effect. Chen Qiling now holds the claim of 41,000,000 yuan and corresponding interest against Huang Ming in the aforementioned case, and the amount of the acquired claim is far higher than the amount of the debt in question. Pursuant to Article 99 of the Contract Law, both the debt in question and the claim acquired by Chen Qiling are matured claims, the subject matter is monetary debt, and neither falls under the circumstances where set-off is prohibited by law or the nature of the contract. Therefore, Chen Qiling is entitled to claim set-off of the debt, and the debt in question has already been set off.

The respondent Huang Ming argued in reply: 1. Regarding the issue of the "Settlement Plan" signed by Huang Ming and Chen Zefeng. (1) The "Settlement Plan" signed by Huang Ming and Chen Zefeng on January 22, 2018, was intended to release Chen Zefeng's guaranty liability, but Chen Zefeng ultimately did not perform the "Settlement Plan." (2) Chen Qiling and others requested set-off of the debt, indicating that they had abandoned the "Settlement Plan." (3) The background for signing the "Settlement Plan" was that Huang Ming had preserved the factory buildings and land of the company controlled by Chen Zefeng, causing difficulties in Chen Zefeng's operations. Chen Zefeng approached Huang Ming requesting partial payment and release of his liability, so Huang Ming agreed to sign the "Settlement Plan." Based on the above three points, the "Settlement Plan" is not binding on Huang Ming. 2. The first instance judgment correctly applied the law in rejecting Chen Qiling's claim to set off the debt in this case by acquiring the claims of a third party, and should be upheld. The debtor corresponding to Chen Qiling's claim is Huang Ming and Xie Suyue. Xie Suyue and Huang Ming are husband and wife. The claim in this case of Huang Ming is not a joint spousal claim, so Chen Qiling's claim for set-off has no legal basis; Huang Ming is involved in a debt dispute due to a triangular debt. Currently, as an enforcement respondent, he has multiple enforcement cases pending and cannot fulfill his debts. If set-off is permitted, it would place the claim of the third party Wu Yongzhong in a position of priority satisfaction, harming the interests of other creditors. The first instance judgment had clear facts and correctly applied the law. Therefore, the appellant's appeal should be dismissed and the original judgment affirmed.

In the first instance, Huang Ming filed the following claims with Fujian High Court: 1. Order the defendant Chen Qiling to immediately repay the plaintiff the outstanding loan principal of RMB 35,000,000; 2. Order the defendant Chen Qiling to pay the plaintiff interest from November 2, 2013, to the date of actual repayment [as of September 27, 2016, the outstanding interest was provisionally calculated as RMB 24,749,333.33 (see detailed interest calculation list)]; 3. Order the defendant Chen Qiling to pay the plaintiff attorney's fees of RMB 80,000; The total of items 1, 2, and 3 above amounts to RMB 59,829,333.33. 4. Order the defendants Chen Zefeng and Fengquan Company to bear joint and several liability for Chen Qiling's above debts; 5. Order the three defendants to bear the case acceptance fee, announcement fee, and preservation fee. During the trial, Huang Ming amended the third claim to: Request the court to order the defendant Chen Qiling to pay the plaintiff attorney's fees of RMB 150,000.

The court of first instance found the following facts: On June 23, 2013, the defendant Chen Qiling, as the borrower, issued a "Loan Receipt" to the plaintiff Huang Ming. The "Loan Receipt" stated: Upon verification and confirmation, as of June 23, 2013, the cumulative outstanding loan from Huang Ming was 35,000,000 yuan, with a monthly interest rate of 3.5%, interest payable before the 22nd of each month, a loan term of 12 months, and in case of overdue repayment, a penalty of 0.5% per day of the loan amount. The guarantors Fengquan Company and Chen Zefeng voluntarily provided joint and several guaranty for the borrower's above loan, with a guarantee period from the date of signing this receipt to two years after the loan term expires. The scope of guarantee includes the loan principal, interest, overdue penalty, and expenses paid by the lender to realize the claim. The borrower and guarantors agreed to bear the expenses incurred by the lender to realize the claim (including but not limited to attorney's fees, notary fees, litigation fees, travel expenses, and other actual expenses for realizing the claim). Thereafter, the plaintiff agreed to extend the repayment period to March 23, 2015. On March 23, 2015, Chen Zefeng and Fengquan Company again confirmed on the receipt that they guaranteed the above loan to Chen Qiling "until the principal and interest are fully repaid."

From June 29, 2013, to September 11, 2016, the defendant Chen Qiling made 19 payments of interest to the plaintiff. Among them, on June 29, 2013, she paid 200,000 yuan; on August 22, 2013, 4,800,000 yuan; on October 14, 2013, 150,000 yuan; on December 4, 2013, 100,000 yuan; on December 18, 2013, 100,000 yuan; on December 27, 2013, 2,200,000 yuan; on January 29, 2014, 500,000 yuan; on February 28, 2014, 100,000 yuan; on March 25, 2014, 300,000 yuan; on April 3, 2014, 500,000 yuan; on May 27, 2014, 1,000,000 yuan; on August 27, 2014, 100,000 yuan; on September 30, 2014, 200,000 yuan; on November 3, 2014, 100,000 yuan; on December 30, 2014, 100,000 yuan; on February 16, 2015, 1,000,000 yuan; on November 27, 2015, 100,000 yuan; on February 6, 2016, 200,000 yuan; on September 11, 2016, 200,000 yuan. The total of the above 19 payments was 11,950,000 yuan.

It was also found that from July 22, 2011, to October 19, 2011, the third party Xie Suyue made payments totaling 56,600,000 yuan via bank transfer to the defendant Chen Qiling's account. On October 10, 2011, Xiamen Mingshengyuan Investment Co., Ltd. made a payment totaling 17,000,000 yuan via bank transfer to the defendant Fengquan Company. From February 2, 2010, to August 9, 2011, the plaintiff Huang Ming made payments totaling 1,000,000 yuan via bank transfer to the defendant Chen Qiling. From October 10, 2011, to October 19, 2011, the plaintiff Huang Ming made payments totaling 15,400,000 yuan via bank transfer to the defendant Chen Qiling.

The third party Huang Kunjin paid attorney's fees of 80,000 yuan and 70,000 yuan to Beijing Dacheng (Xiamen) Law Firm and Fujian Huide (Xiamen) Law Firm, respectively, on September 26, 2016, and March 7, 2018.

It was further found that the plaintiff Huang Ming and Xie Suyue are husband and wife, and Huang Kunjin is his son. The legal representative of Xiamen Mingshengyuan Investment Co., Ltd. is Huang Ming.

The court of first instance held that this case is a dispute over private lending. Since the defendant Chen Zefeng is a resident of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, this case is a civil or commercial dispute involving Hong Kong. Both parties agreed to apply mainland law. Pursuant to Article 19 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Law of the People's Republic of China on the Application of Laws to Foreign-Related Civil Relations (I) and Article 3 of the Law of the People's Republic of China on the Application of Laws to Foreign-Related Civil Relations, mainland law shall apply to this case.

The issues in dispute in this case are: 1. Whether the plaintiff actually lent 35,000,000 yuan to the defendant; 2. Whether the defendant still owed the plaintiff interest of 6,576,000 yuan when the IOU in question was issued on June 23, 2013; 3. Whether the monthly interest rate of 3.5% stipulated in the "Loan Receipt" exceeded the statutory interest rate standard, and whether the interest of 11,950,000 yuan already repaid by the defendant should be deducted from the principal; 4. The amount of attorney's fees the defendant should bear for the plaintiff; 5. Whether the defendant can set off the debt in this case by acquiring the claims of a third party. In this regard, the court of first instance analyzed and determined as follows:

1. Whether the plaintiff actually lent 35,000,000 yuan to the defendant

According to the "Loan Receipt" issued by the defendant Chen Qiling to the plaintiff Huang Ming on June 23, 2013, both parties confirmed after verification that as of June 23, 2013, the defendant Chen Qiling had an outstanding cumulative loan of 35,000,000 yuan from the plaintiff Huang Ming. The defendants Fengquan Company and Chen Zefeng, as guarantors, also stamped and signed the receipt, and all parties clearly acknowledged the facts of the loan. On March 23, 2015, the defendants Chen Zefeng and Fengquan Company again confirmed on the receipt that they guaranteed the above loan to Chen Qiling "until the principal and interest are fully repaid," reaffirming the facts of the loan. The evidence provided by the plaintiff Huang Ming also showed that from July 22, 2011, to October 19, 2011, he made payments totaling 90,000,000 yuan to the bank accounts of the defendant Chen Qiling or Fengquan Company through his own account or accounts of third parties. The defendants failed to prove that the above remittances were unrelated to the loan in question; on the contrary, they claimed that they had repaid interest of 11,950,000 yuan, which further proves that the loan in question actually occurred. Therefore, the defendant's claim that the loan in question was not actually performed cannot be sustained.

2. Whether the defendant Chen Qiling still owed the plaintiff interest of 6,576,000 yuan when the IOU in question was issued on June 23, 2013

The parties confirmed the amount of outstanding loan principal in the "Loan Receipt" but did not mention that the defendant Chen Qiling still owed interest. The plaintiff explained that the interest was calculated based on prior loans. However, the plaintiff Huang Ming brought this lawsuit based on the "Loan Receipt" in question. The interest arising from loans made before the issuance of the "Loan Receipt" is unrelated to this case and should be resolved separately by the parties. Therefore, the plaintiff's claim for the defendant Chen Qiling to repay the interest of 6,576,000 yuan has no factual basis, and the court of first instance did not support it.

3. Whether the monthly interest rate stipulated in the "Loan Receipt" exceeded the statutory interest rate standard, and whether the interest of 11,950,000 yuan already repaid by the defendant Chen Qiling can be deducted from the principal

Article 26 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Private Lending Cases stipulates that if the interest rate agreed upon by the parties does not exceed 24% per annum, the lender's request for the borrower to pay interest at the agreed rate shall be supported by the people's court; if the agreed interest rate exceeds 36% per annum, the agreement on the excess interest is invalid. If the borrower requests the return of the portion of interest already paid that exceeds 36% per annum, the people's court shall support it. The monthly interest rate of 3.5% stipulated in the "Loan Receipt" in question exceeds 36% per annum, and the agreement on the excess interest is invalid. The defendant Chen Qiling paid a total of 11,950,000 yuan to the plaintiff between June 29, 2013, and September 11, 2016. Among them, the repayment of 200,000 yuan on June 29, 2013: at an annual interest rate of 36%, based on the outstanding principal of 35,000,000 yuan, the interest was 7,123.29 yuan; the repayment of 4,800,000 yuan on August 22, 2013: after deducting the interest calculated at 36% per annum of 1,871,232.18 yuan, the remainder of 2,928,767.82 yuan was deducted from the principal, leaving an outstanding principal of 32,071,232.18 yuan. Thereafter, the remaining interest payments of 6,950,000 yuan made by Chen Qiling from October 14, 2013, to September 11, 2016, when calculated at 36% per annum, can cover 220 days of interest, i.e., the interest paid is deemed to have been paid up to March 30, 2014. From March 31, 2014, interest shall be calculated at 24% per annum.

4. The amount of attorney's fees for the plaintiff's authorized agent that the defendant should bear

The "Loan Receipt" in question stipulates that the defendants Chen Zefeng and Fengquan Company shall bear joint and several guaranty liability for the debts of the defendant Chen Qiling, with the scope of guarantee including the loan principal, interest, overdue penalty, and expenses incurred by the lender to realize the claim. The three defendants also confirmed that the borrower and guarantors agreed to bear various expenses, including attorney's fees, incurred by the lender to realize the claim. Therefore, the defendants should bear the reasonable expenses incurred by the plaintiff for this lawsuit. The plaintiff Huang Ming successively engaged lawyers from Beijing Dacheng (Xiamen) Law Firm and Fujian Huide Law Firm to represent him in this lawsuit and paid attorney's fees of 80,000 yuan and 70,000 yuan, respectively. Since the plaintiff terminated the agency contract with the lawyer from Beijing Dacheng (Xiamen) Law Firm, and that lawyer did not complete the agency work, the fees arising from that contract are not reasonable expenses incurred by the plaintiff to realize the claim and should not be supported. Therefore, the defendant Chen Qiling shall only bear liability for 70,000 yuan of the above attorney's fees.

5. Whether the defendant can set off the debt in this case by acquiring the claims of a third party

The creditor-debtor relationship between the plaintiff Huang Ming and a third party is not the same legal relationship as this case. Moreover, the plaintiff does not agree to set off the debt between him and the third party against the debt owed by the defendant. Therefore, the defendant's claim to set off the debt in this case by acquiring the claims of a third party is not supported by the court of first instance.

The "Loan Receipt" in question reflects the true intention of the contracting parties. Except for the interest rate exceeding 36% per annum, which renders the agreement on the excess interest invalid, the other contents of the contract do not violate prohibitive provisions of laws and regulations and should be deemed lawful and valid. The defendant Chen Qiling failed to pay interest in accordance with the law and contract, and also failed to repay the principal and corresponding interest after the loan term expired. She should bear liability for breach of contract. The defendants Chen Zefeng and Fengquan Company voluntarily assumed joint and several guaranty liability for the above debts of the defendant Chen Qiling, with the scope of guarantee including the loan principal, interest, overdue penalty, and expenses incurred by the lender to realize the claim. Therefore, the defendants Chen Zefeng and Fengquan Company shall bear joint and several guaranty liability within the above scope of guarantee.

In summary, in accordance with Article 19 of the Interpretation (I) of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Law of the PRC on Choice of Law for Foreign-Related Civil Relations, Article 3 of the Law of the PRC on Choice of Law for Foreign-Related Civil Relations, Article 60, paragraph 1, Article 107, Article 205, Article 206, and Article 207 of the Contract Law of the PRC, Article 12, Article 18, and Article 31 of the Guarantee Law of the PRC, Article 26 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Private Lending Cases, and Article 42, paragraph 1 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Guarantee Law of the PRC, the judgment is as follows: 1. The defendant, Chen Qiling, shall, within ten days from the date this judgment becomes effective, repay to the plaintiff, Huang Ming, the outstanding principal of the loan in the amount of RMB 32,071,232.18, and pay interest calculated on the basis of RMB 32,071,232.18 at an annual rate of 24% from March 31, 2014 to the date of actual payment; 2. The defendant, Chen Qiling, shall, within ten days from the date this judgment becomes effective, pay to the plaintiff, Huang Ming, the attorney's fee of RMB 70,000; 3. The defendants, Chen Zefeng and Fengquan Company, shall bear joint and several liability for repayment of the aforesaid debts of the defendant, Chen Qiling. After assuming the guaranty liability, Chen Zefeng and Fengquan Company have the right to seek recourse from the defendant, Chen Qiling; 4. The other claims of the plaintiff, Huang Ming, are dismissed. The case acceptance fee of RMB 340,946.66 shall be borne by the defendants, Chen Qiling, Chen Zefeng, and Fengquan Company in the amount of RMB 292,518.99, and by the plaintiff, Huang Ming, in the amount of RMB 48,427.67. The litigation preservation fee of RMB 5,000 shall be borne by the defendants, Chen Qiling, Chen Zefeng, and Fengquan Company.

During the second instance of this court, the parties submitted evidence in accordance with the law regarding the grounds of appeal. This court organized the parties to exchange and examine the evidence. Chen Qiling, Chen Zefeng, and Fengquan Company submitted a special voucher of the payment system, intending to prove that after Chen Qiling received the funds from Huang Ming, she transferred them to Fengquan Company, and therefore Chen Zefeng and Fengquan Company were the actual borrowers of the loan involved in the case. Huang Ming submitted the results of an inquiry into his status as a judgment debtor in multiple enforcement cases, intending to prove that, as a judgment debtor in multiple enforcement cases, he was unable to repay his debts, and that the debt set-off claim raised by Chen Qiling would harm the interests of Huang Ming's other creditors. This court is of the opinion that the evidence submitted by Chen Qiling, Chen Zefeng, and Fengquan Company cannot prove the fact they sought to prove, i.e., that Chen Zefeng and Fengquan Company were the actual borrowers in this case, and this court does not recognize it. The evidence submitted by Huang Ming can prove that Huang Ming is a judgment debtor in multiple enforcement cases.

This court confirms the facts found at first instance in accordance with the law. The following facts were found upon trial in the second instance:

1. On January 22, 2018, Chen Zefeng (Party A) and Huang Ming (Party B) executed a Settlement Proposal, which provided: I. As of December 31, 2017, Party A owed Party B a principal of RMB 35 million, with interest calculated at 2% and the remaining interest at RMB 16.8 million. After negotiation by the parties, the principal and interest are determined to be settled at RMB 40 million; II. Payment method: 1. Within one month from the date of signing the agreement, RMB 20 million shall be paid; 2. By December 31, 2018, Party A shall pay RMB 10 million, and pay interest on the RMB 10 million at the bank loan interest rate; 3. By December 31, 2019, the remaining RMB 10 million shall be paid, and interest on the RMB 10 million from January 1, 2018 to December 31, 2019 shall be paid at the bank loan interest rate. III. If Party A violates the foregoing payment method, Party A shall bear liquidated damages at an annual rate of 24%. After Chen Zefeng and Huang Ming signed the Settlement Proposal, on the last day of the payment period for the first installment of RMB 20 million (February 22, 2018), Chen Zefeng sent a Reminder Letter to Huang Ming, requesting Huang Ming to provide a bank account for receiving the payment. Chen Zefeng never performed his repayment obligation in the following two years.

2. In the loan dispute between Huang Ming and his wife Xie Suyue and the third party Wu Yongzhong, the final judgment of the Fujian High People's Court [(2015) Min Min Zhong Zi No. 2259] confirmed: "Huang Ming and Xie Suyue shall, within ten days from the date this judgment becomes effective, repay Wu Yongzhong RMB 41 million in loan principal and interest (calculated from November 1, 2011 on the basis of RMB 41 million principal at four times the benchmark interest rate of the same type of bank loan for the same period until the date of repayment; the amount already paid of RMB 1,806,322 shall be offset against the interest)." On October 11, 2016, Wu Yongzhong applied to the Xiamen Intermediate People's Court for enforcement of the above case, but due to the absence of actual enforceable property of Huang Ming and Xie Suyue, the Xiamen Intermediate People's Court terminated the enforcement. In addition to the enforcement case with Wu Yongzhong, Huang Ming is also a judgment debtor in multiple other cases in which he is involved, and because Huang Ming has no property available for enforcement, he has been included in the list of dishonest persons subject to enforcement by the court.

3. On May 22, 2018, Wu Yongzhong and Chen Qiling executed a Confirmation of Assignment of Creditor's Rights, agreeing that Wu Yongzhong would assign to Chen Qiling the principal and interest of the creditor's rights of RMB 41 million that he held against Huang Ming, and on the same day, a Notice of Assignment of Creditor's Rights was sent to Huang Ming and Xie Suyue. Huang Ming and Xie Suyue received the above notice on May 25, 2018. Chen Qiling claimed on August 21, 2018 (during the first instance proceedings) to set off the creditor's rights she had acquired from Wu Yongzhong against her debts to Huang Ming.

This court is of the opinion that this case is a dispute over a private loan. Because Chen Zefeng is a resident of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, this case is a civil and commercial dispute involving Hong Kong. Both parties agree that the laws of the mainland shall apply to this case. Pursuant to Article 19 of the Interpretation (I) of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Law of the PRC on Choice of Law for Foreign-Related Civil Relations and Article 3 of the Law of the PRC on Choice of Law for Foreign-Related Civil Relations, the laws of the mainland shall apply to this case.

The issues in dispute in this case are: 1. Whether the appellants' claim for determining the principal and interest in this case in accordance with the Settlement Proposal should be upheld; 2. Whether the creditor's rights assigned to Chen Qiling by the third party Wu Yongzhong can be set off against her debts to Huang Ming. This court's analysis and determination are as follows:

1. Whether the appellants' claim for determining the principal and interest in this case in accordance with the Settlement Proposal should be upheld

(1) Whether the validity of the Settlement Proposal extends to Chen Qiling

The Settlement Proposal was executed by Huang Ming and Chen Zefeng. Both parties acknowledge that the Settlement Proposal was executed on the basis of the disputes involved in the case, represents the true intention of both parties, does not violate the prohibitive provisions of laws and administrative regulations, and is legally valid and effective. Although Chen Zefeng, Chen Qiling, and Fengquan Company claim that Chen Zefeng signed the Settlement Proposal on behalf of the three parties jointly, and that the Settlement Proposal constitutes a re-confirmation of the creditor's rights and debts involved in the case, the Settlement Proposal does not bear the signature or seal of the debtor Chen Qiling or the guarantor Fengquan Company, nor does the Settlement Proposal contain any expression that Chen Zefeng signed on behalf of the three parties. The creditor Huang Ming also does not acknowledge that the Settlement Proposal discharged Chen Qiling's debts. Therefore, this agreement cannot constitute an exempted assumption of debt; Chen Zefeng merely joined the debt involved in the case as a co-debtor. Furthermore, because Chen Qiling raised a claim for debt set-off against Huang Ming using the creditor's rights she had acquired during the first instance, it is evident that Chen Qiling did not consider that the Settlement Proposal had discharged her repayment obligation. In summary, the Settlement Proposal cannot constitute a re-confirmation of the creditor's rights and debts involved in the case, nor does it discharge Chen Qiling's debts. The Loan Receipt shall still be the basis for confirming the creditor's rights and debts involved in the case.

(2) Whether the principal and interest of Chen Zefeng's guaranteed creditor's rights can be determined in accordance with the Settlement Proposal

In this case, the Settlement Proposal stipulated that Chen Zefeng should pay Huang Ming RMB 20 million by February 22, 2018, RMB 10 million and interest by December 31, 2018, and RMB 10 million and interest by December 31, 2019, but Chen Zefeng did not pay the corresponding amounts within the agreed time limit or thereafter. On the last day of the payment period for the first installment of RMB 20 million, Chen Zefeng sent a Reminder Letter to Huang Ming requesting Huang Ming to provide a bank account for receiving the payment, and did not perform the repayment obligation within the two years after the first repayment period expired. Moreover, because the Settlement Proposal was executed during the litigation of this case, Chen Zefeng could have applied to the court for deposit of the funds to discharge the debt and perform his contractual obligations, but Chen Zefeng did not repay the debt in this manner. The above facts are sufficient to show Chen Zefeng's true intention to refuse repayment. Although the Settlement Proposal did not clearly specify the bank account for repaying Huang Ming, this defect does not constitute an obstacle to Chen Zefeng's performance. Therefore, the defense raised by Chen Zefeng that he was unable to repay because Huang Ming did not provide a bank account, and that his sending of a Reminder Letter requesting Huang Ming to inform him of the bank account was sufficient to prove that Chen Zefeng did not breach the contract, is untenable. Chen Zefeng did not perform the debt determined in the Settlement Proposal as a co-debtor within the agreed time limit. The court of first instance determined his guaranty liability in accordance with the Loan Receipt, which was not improper.

2. Whether Chen Qiling's claim to set off the creditor's rights she acquired from the third party Wu Yongzhong against Huang Ming's debts to her

First, the people's court shall review the set-off claim raised by the parties. The debt set-off claim raised by Chen Qiling in the first instance constitutes a defense against Huang Ming's claim for creditor's rights by exercising the right of set-off, i.e., a set-off defense in litigation. Generally, it is legally not improper for a defendant to raise a set-off defense in litigation during the proceedings. To achieve the goal of litigation economy and to relieve the parties of the burden of filing a separate lawsuit in individual cases, the people's court shall review and handle the set-off defense raised by the defendant in the case and determine whether this defense is established. The court of first instance, on the grounds that the creditor-debtor relationship between Huang Ming and the third party Wu Yongzhong is not the same legal relationship as this case and that Huang Ming did not agree to set off his debt with Wu Yongzhong against Chen Qiling's debt, failed to review Chen Qiling's set-off claim. This was improper, and this court points it out here.

Second, the exercise of the right of set-off shall not harm the lawful rights and interests of third parties. The right of set-off is a substantive right provided by the Contract Law. A debtor may discharge his own debt and realize his creditor's rights by exercising the right of set-off, but the exercise of the right of set-off shall not harm the lawful rights and interests of third parties. To this end, while recognizing the right of set-off, the Enterprise Bankruptcy Law of the PRC also imposes restrictions on the active creditor's rights used for set-off, in particular providing that a debtor's debtor who, after the acceptance of the bankruptcy application, acquires a creditor's right from others against the debtor, or who acquires a creditor's right against the debtor knowing that the debtor is unable to repay its debts as they fall due or that the bankruptcy application has been filed, is not allowed to set off. The main purpose of this system is to prevent, when the debtor is insolvent, the debtor's debtor from acquiring new creditor's rights and claiming set-off, thereby giving priority satisfaction to the newly acquired creditor's rights and discharging its own debts, to the detriment of the interests of other creditors. Similarly, under the current judicial situation in China, where there is no natural person bankruptcy law and where litigation proceedings and enforcement proceedings are related, when an individual debtor is unable to repay its debts as they fall due, harm to the lawful rights and interests of third parties, especially other creditors of the individual debtor, should be prevented. Because Huang Ming is already a judgment debtor in multiple enforcement cases, and the creditor's rights in these cases have not been satisfied due to the lack of property available for enforcement by Huang Ming, if Chen Qiling is permitted in this case to set off the debt with the acquired creditor's rights, this will directly reduce the property available for enforcement by Huang Ming and harm the lawful interests of other creditors in other enforcement cases involving Huang Ming.

Third, the exercise of the right of set-off in litigation proceedings shall not conflict with the principle of fair distribution in enforcement proceedings. In general, a valid set-off defense in litigation may be upheld after review by the court, but when the exercise of the right of set-off in litigation proceedings is related to the participation in distribution in enforcement proceedings, the exercise of the right of set-off should be subject to certain restrictions. In this case, Huang Ming, as a judgment debtor in multiple enforcement cases, has been unable to perform his debts. The active creditor's right acquired by Chen Qiling and claimed for set-off originated from one of these enforcement cases, and that creditor's right had previously been subject to compulsory termination of enforcement due to the absence of property available for enforcement by Huang Ming. If Chen Qiling is permitted in this case to set off the debt with the acquired creditor's rights, this means that the creditor's right derived from Wu Yongzhong, which could not be satisfied through enforcement, would instead be indirectly given priority satisfaction over Huang Ming's other creditors in this manner, directly conflicting with the principle of fair distribution under the system of participation in distribution in enforcement proceedings.

Finally, the people's court shall determine whether to uphold the exercise of the right of set-off in accordance with the principle of good faith. Where a debtor claims set-off with creditor's rights acquired through assignment, and the acquired creditor's rights cannot be realized in enforcement proceedings, the people's court shall conduct a careful substantive review of the set-off defense in litigation. That is, the people's court shall review the acquisition of the active creditor's rights used for set-off in accordance with the principle of good faith, so as to protect bona fide set-off rights while not harming the lawful rights and interests of third parties. In this case, where Chen Qiling knew that Huang Ming, as a judgment debtor in multiple cases, lacked property available for enforcement, her act of acquiring the creditor's rights after the first instance trial of this case and claiming set-off violates the principle of good faith. Furthermore, if Chen Qiling can produce evidence to prove that Huang Ming actually still has other property available for enforcement, and that the set-off defense in litigation will not in fact harm the interests of other creditors of the judgment debtor outside the case, the court may still uphold such a set-off defense in litigation. However, Chen Qiling failed to provide valid evidence to prove that Huang Ming still has sufficient other property available for enforcement, nor did she prove that her set-off defense in litigation would not in result harm the interests of Huang Ming's other creditors outside the case. Therefore, this court does not uphold Chen Qiling's set-off defense in litigation.

In summary, the appeal requests of Chen Qiling, Chen Zefeng, and Fengquan Company lack factual and legal basis, cannot be established, and should be dismissed. Pursuant to Article 170, paragraph 1, item (1) of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC and Article 334 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, the judgment is as follows:

The appeal is dismissed and the original judgment is affirmed.

The case acceptance fee for the second instance of RMB 340,946.66 shall be borne by Chen Qiling, Chen Zefeng, and Fujian Fengquan Environmental Protection Group Co., Ltd.

This judgment is final.
